_doc: HMTc Category 34 (Herbs, Spices, Seasonings and Salt) compiler config. Method v2.0 (government-limit default). Every cell names EXPLICIT register ids (a LOOKUP, not a computation); occurrence never selects a number. This is the lead-in-spices enforcement space — the highest-salience adulteration category in the program (turmeric/chili lead-chromate adulteration; recent recalls) — so basis discipline is load-bearing: DRIED-spice limits govern (dried-basis), and fresh fruiting-vegetable / fresh-leaf-vegetable limits (e.g. Israel fruiting-vegetable Pb 50 incl. bell pepper; MERCOSUR fresh-herb 300) are the WRONG basis for a dried spice and are excluded. Lead in spices binds EU Reg. 2023/915, which splits by botanical part (fruit 600 / seed 900 / flower-pistil 1000 / bud 1000 / root-rhizome 1500 / bark 2000) — carried as a form_split, preserved exactly; certification applies the part matching the spice (turmeric=root/rhizome, cinnamon=bark, paprika/chili/pepper=fruit, cumin=seed). Salt lead binds EU 2023/915 split refined (1000) vs unrefined (2000). Because turmeric/chili adulteration is lead-CHROMATE (PbCrO4), total chromium and Cr-VI are SCREENED (control) as adulteration co-markers with lead in the plant-derived rows, not dismissed. Panel: 8 totals (Pb, Cd, tAs, tHg, Ni, Sn, Al, total Cr) + species controls (iAs, Cr-VI); MeHg is not-material (no marine-bioaccumulation pathway in a dry spice or a mineral). See docs/governance for the Cat-7-dissolution Step-0 event that created Cat 34.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; explicit-id lookup; legislated product-form splits preserved; dried-spice basis discipline)

spices.name: Herbs, spices, and dried seasonings (turmeric, cinnamon, paprika, chili powder, pepper)
spices.native_basis_label: dried spice as placed on the market (dry basis)
spices.audit_exclude_scope: fresh|fruiting vegetable|leaf vegetable|leafy vegetable|loose-leaf|vegetables and fruit|vegetables general|vegetables excluding|curry powder|\bsalt\b|\btea\b|\boil\b|seed oil

form_split.basis: dried spice as placed on the market (dry basis)
form_split.instrument: EU Reg. 2023/915 — lead in spices, set by botanical part. The controlling worldwide instrument for spice lead; carried as a form_split and preserved exactly. Certification applies the botanical part matching the spice.

forms.form: fruit spices (paprika, chili powder, black pepper, allspice)

Cd.basis_label: dried spice (dry basis); spice-specific dried-basis limit. Fresh fruiting-vegetable Cd (50) and fresh-herb Cd (200) are a different, wet-weight basis and do not govern a dried spice.

tAs.basis_label: dried herbs and spices (dry basis). Fresh-herb tAs (300) is a wet-weight basis and does not govern a dried spice.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets an inorganic-arsenic maximum level specific to dried spices (inorganic arsenic is a dietary speciation defined for rice and drinking water); dried-spice arsenic is regulated as total arsenic, which arithmetically bounds the inorganic fraction (iAs <= tAs). The New York State DOH 2019 metals-in-spices guidance (nys-doh2019-metals-spices-guidance), routed to this row, reports measurable inorganic arsenic in spices, so the fraction is screened by reflex speciation on the total-As result rather than dismissed as absent. Israel's dried-plant iAs figure (300 ug/kg) is bounded by, and consistent with, the total-As ceiling.
control.reference_method: Reflex inorganic-As speciation on the total-As result; bounded by the tAs cell. No sovereign dried-spice iAs ML.
control.trigger: reflex iAs speciation when total arsenic approaches the tAs ceiling

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is a marine-bioaccumulation speciation with no formation pathway in a terrestrial dried spice, and it is arithmetically bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg). Spice mercury is regulated as total mercury, which the tHg standard caps, bounding any organomercury fraction.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-Hg spice standard (Vietnam, 50 ug/kg); no methylmercury spice ML anywhere

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a nickel maximum level for dried spices. The EU sets nickel only for fresh herbs (1200 ug/kg) and leafy vegetables (500 ug/kg) on a fresh-weight basis; reading either across to a dried spice would be a basis error (drying concentrates the analyte several-fold), so it would UNDERSTATE a protective standard and is not used. Nickel is screened instead of assigned a mis-based number.
control.reference_method: Total-nickel screen (ICP-MS); no dried-spice sovereign ML; EU fresh-herb/leafy-veg nickel limits are fresh-basis and not comparable.
control.trigger: periodic nickel screen; flag on anomalous elevation

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a tin maximum level for dried spices (tin MLs govern tinplate-canned product only). Routed sources (cicero2022-minerals-spices-aromatic-herbs, pradhan2023-heracleum-nepalense-elements) report measurable trace tin in dried spices from soil/processing background, so tin is screened rather than dismissed as absent.
control.reference_method: Total-tin screen (ICP-MS); no sovereign dried-spice tin ML; the canned-food 250 mg/kg limit is can-only.
control.trigger: periodic tin screen; flag on anomalous elevation

not_material.rationale: Dried spices are natural aluminium accumulators (aluminium is taken up from soil and concentrated on drying); the aluminium present is background, not contamination. No credible regulator sets an aluminium contaminant maximum level for spices; dietary aluminium is managed by intake against the EFSA/JECFA TWI, not by a per-food ML. Matches the existing spices/Al determination in standards-not-material.csv.
not_material.reference_method: Managed by intake vs TWI; periodic screen; no per-food contaminant ML.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No Al contaminant ML for spices in any credible jurisdiction; managed by TWI
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (lists no Al); Codex; FSANZ; JECFA/EFSA TWI

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a total-chromium food maximum level (chromium(III) is an essential nutrient). For spices this cell is load-bearing as an ADULTERATION SCREEN, not a nutrient check: turmeric and chili powder are adulterated with lead chromate (PbCrO4) to brighten colour, so an elevated total chromium co-occurring with elevated lead is the signature of lead-chromate adulteration. Total chromium is screened and co-read with the lead result.
control.reference_method: Total-chromium screen (ICP-MS), co-read with lead; substrate for reflex Cr-VI speciation.
control.trigger: flag when total chromium is elevated and co-occurs with elevated lead (lead-chromate adulteration signature)

control.rationale: Lead chromate (PbCrO4) used to adulterate turmeric and chili is a hexavalent-chromium compound, so Cr-VI is NOT dismissed as not-material for spices (unlike inert food matrices where Cr-VI reduces to Cr-III). Where the lead/total-chromium adulteration screen is elevated, reflex Cr-VI speciation confirms the chromate. No sovereign sets a Cr-VI food ML, so this is a screen, not an alignment.
control.reference_method: Reflex Cr-VI speciation triggered by the lead-chromate adulteration signature (elevated lead + elevated total chromium).
control.trigger: reflex Cr-VI speciation on the lead-chromate adulteration signature

spices.scope_note: Covers dried herbs, spices, and dried seasonings (turmeric, cinnamon, paprika, chili powder, pepper, cumin, etc.). Lead is a form_split by EU botanical part (fruit/seed/flower-pistil/bud/root-rhizome/bark). Total chromium and Cr-VI are screened as lead-chromate adulteration co-markers, the defining hazard of this category. Fresh culinary herbs sold fresh route to the produce categories; tea and herbal infusions route to Cat 5 Beverages; salt routes to the salt row.

salt.name: Salt (table, sea, Himalayan)
salt.native_basis_label: food-grade salt as placed on the market (dry)

form_split.basis: food-grade salt as placed on the market (dry)
form_split.instrument: EU Reg. 2023/915 — lead in salt, split refined (general food-grade) vs unrefined (fleur de sel, grey salt, manually harvested). The strictest sovereign salt-lead limit; Codex STAN 193 sets 2 mg/kg, so the EU refined value governs.

forms.form: unrefined salt (fleur de sel, grey salt, manually harvested sea salt)

Cd.basis_label: food-grade salt (dry); Codex-aligned 0.5 mg/kg, concurred by many jurisdictions

tAs.basis_label: food-grade salt (dry); total arsenic, EU Reg. 2025/1891 with FSANZ concurrence at 500

subsumed.rationale: No in-force sovereign or general-food iAs maximum level applies to this product on the dietary-content basis after the supersession of regulations/israel-moh-fcs-2016-heavy-metals-tin-food-guidelines; the species is bounded by its parent total (tAs) per the certification-readiness ruling (species ≤ total).

tHg.basis_label: food-grade salt (dry); total mercury, EU Reg. 2022/617 with FSANZ concurrence at 100

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is the organomercury speciation of mercury and is arithmetically bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg); a mineral salt carries no mercury source and no methylmercury formation pathway, and salt mercury is regulated as total mercury, which the tHg standard caps, bounding any organomercury fraction.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-Hg salt standard (EU 2022/617, 100 ug/kg); no methylmercury salt ML anywhere

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a nickel maximum level for salt. Unrefined rock and sea salts can carry trace geologic nickel; it is screened rather than assigned an invented number.
control.reference_method: Total-nickel screen (ICP-MS); no sovereign salt nickel ML.
control.trigger: periodic nickel screen; flag on anomalous elevation

not_material.rationale: No tin source in a boxed/bagged mineral salt; tin is a tinplate-can migration pathway only.
not_material.reference_method: Packaging control (non-tinplate); periodic ICP-MS tin verification.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No salt tin ML; canned-food 250 mg/kg limit is can-only

not_material.rationale: Aluminium in salt derives from permitted anti-caking additives (e.g. sodium aluminosilicate, GRAS in US table salt per 21 CFR 182.2727), not contamination, and is managed by additive law plus intake against the EFSA/JECFA TWI, not by a per-food contaminant maximum level. Matches the existing salt/Al determination in standards-not-material.csv.
not_material.reference_method: Managed by additive law + TWI; periodic screen.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Al managed by additive law (US 21 CFR 182.2727; EU 1333/2008) + TWI; no salt contaminant ML
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (lists no Al); US 21 CFR 182.2727; Codex; JECFA/EFSA TWI

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a total-chromium food maximum level (chromium(III) is an essential nutrient). Trace chromium in salt is geologic. Screened as the substrate for reflex Cr-VI speciation.
control.reference_method: Total-chromium screen; substrate for reflex Cr-VI speciation.
control.trigger: reflex Cr-VI speciation only if total chromium is anomalously elevated

not_material.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is the Cr(VI) speciation of chromium and is bounded by the total-chromium control (Cr-VI <= total Cr), which is screened for salt; no jurisdiction sets a Cr-VI food maximum level. There is no chromium adulteration pathway in a mineral salt (unlike turmeric/chili, salt is not colour-adulterated with lead chromate), so any trace chromium is geologic chromium(III). Rebuttable if a routed source reports hexavalent chromium in salt.
not_material.reference_method: Bounded by the total-chromium screen; no routine Cr-VI speciation, reflex only on anomalously elevated total chromium.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No Cr-VI food ML anywhere; bounded by total chromium (Cr-VI <= total Cr); no chromate-adulteration pathway in salt

salt.scope_note: Covers table salt, sea salt, and Himalayan/rock salt. Lead is a form_split refined (1000) vs unrefined (2000) per EU 2023/915; certification applies the form matching the product. Salt is an independent mineral row (not plant-uptake); cadmium/arsenic/mercury bind the Codex-aligned food-grade-salt limits. Aluminium is additive-permitted anti-caking, managed by additive law and TWI.

iAs.rationale: Published iAs of 500 ug/kg is retained as a precautionary program value after the instrument that carried it (il_fcs2016_ias_12_salt_500) was superseded; the strictest in-force sovereign floor is the parent total that bounds iAs. HMTc is a ratcheting program and does not loosen a live limit because an instrument died.
iAs.decided: 2026-09-02 wwsaid (governance: Decisions enacted under standing permission)

hot-chili-sauces.native_basis_label: sauce as placed on the market (as-consumed liquid)

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is the organomercury speciation of mercury and is arithmetically bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg); a chili/vinegar/water sauce carries no mercury source and no methylmercury formation pathway, and it is bounded by the total-mercury sauce limit.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-Hg sauce standard (Vietnam, 50 ug/kg); no methylmercury sauce ML anywhere

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a nickel maximum level for sauces. Screened rather than assigned an invented number.
control.reference_method: Total-nickel screen (ICP-MS); no sovereign sauce nickel ML.
control.trigger: periodic nickel screen; flag on anomalous elevation

not_material.rationale: Hot/chili sauces are sold in glass or plastic bottles, not tinplate cans, so there is no tin source or migration route. Material only for tin-plated canned product.
not_material.reference_method: Packaging control (non-tinplate); periodic ICP-MS tin verification.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No non-canned sauce tin ML; canned-food 250 mg/kg limit is can-only

control.rationale: Confirmed no-ML (standards-no-ml-confirmed.csv): no government sets an aluminium contaminant maximum level for sauces in any checked jurisdiction (EU 2023/915 lists no Al; Codex; FSANZ; JECFA/EFSA TWI). Aluminium in a chili/vinegar/water sauce is chili-borne background plus any permitted additive; dietary aluminium is managed by weekly intake against the EFSA/JECFA TWI, not by a per-food maximum level, so aluminium is screened rather than aligned to a sovereign number. A sauce is not an accumulating crop, so the spice/bouillon natural-accumulator basis does not apply; this is a material-but-unregulated cell (literature-baseline governs), not a not-material claim.
control.reference_method: Total-aluminium screen (ICP-MS); managed by intake vs the EFSA/JECFA TWI; no per-food contaminant ML to align to.
control.trigger: periodic aluminium screen; flag on anomalous elevation

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a total-chromium food maximum level. As with turmeric, chili-borne lead-chromate adulteration is the material chromium pathway for a chili sauce, so total chromium is screened and co-read with lead as an adulteration co-marker.
control.reference_method: Total-chromium screen (ICP-MS), co-read with lead; substrate for reflex Cr-VI speciation.
control.trigger: flag when total chromium is elevated and co-occurs with elevated lead (lead-chromate adulteration signature)

control.rationale: Lead chromate (a hexavalent-chromium compound) used to adulterate chili is the material Cr-VI pathway for a chili sauce, so Cr-VI is screened, not dismissed. Reflex Cr-VI speciation confirms the chromate where the lead/total-chromium adulteration screen is elevated. No sovereign Cr-VI food ML exists.
control.reference_method: Reflex Cr-VI speciation on the lead-chromate adulteration signature.
control.trigger: reflex Cr-VI speciation on the lead-chromate adulteration signature

hot-chili-sauces.scope_note: Covers hot sauces and chili sauces. Routed here (not Cat 32 Condiments) because their lead and chromium are chili-borne, the same lead-chromate adulteration platform as turmeric. Contaminant limits bind the finished-sauce (liquid, as-consumed) sovereign limits; total chromium and Cr-VI are adulteration screens. Soy sauce and fish sauce route to Cat 32.

not_material.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the read-across total-Hg standard (50); no methylmercury blend ML anywhere

not_material.regulatory_basis: No dry-blend tin ML; canned-food 250 mg/kg limit is can-only

Consistent with the spices/Al and salt/Al determinations.
not_material.reference_method: Managed by intake vs TWI + additive law; periodic screen.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No Al contaminant ML for seasoning blends; managed by TWI + additive law
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (lists no Al); Codex; FSANZ; JECFA/EFSA TWI

control.rationale: No total-chromium food maximum level in any jurisdiction. Chili/paprika-forward seasoning blends carry the same lead-chromate adulteration risk as whole spices, so total chromium is screened and co-read with lead as an adulteration co-marker.
control.reference_method: Total-chromium screen (ICP-MS), co-read with lead; substrate for reflex Cr-VI speciation.

control.rationale: Chili/paprika seasoning blends can carry lead-chromate (hexavalent-chromium) adulteration, so Cr-VI is screened, not dismissed. Reflex Cr-VI speciation confirms the chromate where the lead/total-chromium screen is elevated. No sovereign Cr-VI food ML exists.
control.reference_method: Reflex Cr-VI speciation on the lead-chromate adulteration signature.
control.trigger: reflex Cr-VI speciation on the lead-chromate adulteration signature

bouillon-seasoning-blends.scope_note: Covers bouillon/stock cubes and powdered seasoning blends (dry rubs, gravy and seasoning packets). No sovereign sets a blend-specific ML, so lead, cadmium, total arsenic and total mercury read across the nearest applicable sovereign scope — the spice-blend / curry-powder limits (curry powder is the archetypal, explicitly-regulated seasoning blend). Chromium is screened as a lead-chromate adulteration co-marker for chili/paprika-forward blends. Salt-dominant bouillon cubes additionally sit at or below the food-grade-salt lead ceiling.
